text:
I don't know if it's thanks to the free (Gold Card) or if it's just my bad luck that I had a day with a doctor who was just plain rude, heavy-handed, and had no encouragement whatsoever. It's unlike other reviews that I'd even like to give a negative review. The star I give is to thank him for allowing me to use my Gold Card.

I had braces elsewhere, and because I had braces, I had a lot of tartar buildup. Other dentists at other clinics charged me 900-1200 baht, so I came here to use my Gold Card. He complained, "You should get your braces done there if you want to have them cleaned. I shouldn't have wasted so much money."

That's right. I'm not unwilling to think that I should do everything at one clinic, get my braces done there. And I'm not unaware that wearing braces makes cleaning difficult and may not be completely clean. We're the patients, we're the ones who are hurt, and we're the ones who suffer if the doctor doesn't do his job properly. Do you think the people who are hurt don't realize it?

But those without money just don't have money. Or are doctors saying, 'If you don't have money, you shouldn't have gotten braces in the first place?' You should know better than anyone that braces can be expensive and it's not just a waste of money. Because if patients had money, they wouldn't have used the gold card for something they were hurting by.

And during the procedure, we were in pain, we cried because it hurt. The doctor said, "You don't have to cry." Seriously, when someone in pain says you don't have to cry...well, can you cry?

I know that if a patient cries, it can make the doctor depressed and afraid to treat them, but what's the point of saying, "You don't have to cry," is that? Do you have a lot of medical experience, but your empathy has all but dried up?

Or is it because it's a gold card? Do poor people have to put up with the mouths and tantrums of medical personnel? And why open a clinic that accepts the gold card if you're going to treat them with this kind of verbal abuse? We don't expect them to pamper you, but if you can't speak nicely to the injured person, it's better to keep quiet. When I went, there weren't many patients, only me, with no queue.

As a doctor, you should know that the injured person is the patient. Why would you keep saying such mean things? And it's so terrible to say it during the procedure. The patient could only hold back, both in pain and having to listen to such harsh words, and couldn't cry because the doctor was depressed and afraid to continue.

But thank you for your harsh words. Because it made the second half of the ordeal of scaling not hurt at all. I was so angry and frustrated with the person who called himself a doctor that I forgot the pain. It was so disgusting.
